claim_text: At least 15,000 veteran families have already been foreclosed on or displaced.
definition: Figure stated by Sen. Blumenthal at SVAC 5/20/26
limitation: Spring 2026 count; no newer figure published; true number likely higher (stale-stats rule)

claim_text: More than 90,000 veteran homeowners are behind on their loans or in the foreclosure process.
definition: NPR/ICE data 4/2/26; NCLC put ~31,500 in active foreclosure
limitation: Spring 2026; stale-stats rule applies

claim_text: About 160,000 veteran families are impacted in total.
definition: Foreclosed + in the pipeline + forced into unaffordable modifications or short sales
limitation: Campaign-compiled sum of the three tiers; not an official single figure; never merge into one number

claim_text: The permanent partial claim was scored as net savings; foreclosure is the more expensive option.
definition: $147 million in net savings over ten years (CBO; H. Rept. 119-104)
limitation: CBO estimate over the ten-year scoring window

claim_text: The average VA foreclosure loss is roughly $72,000 to $74,000.
definition: NCLC ~$72,000; CRL ~$74,000 (~$73,750 per disposition)
limitation: Cite whichever figure with its own source label; do not blend

claim_text: Congress granted permanent partial-claim authority and a directed waterfall; it did not write the exclusionary barriers.
definition: Active-default, current-servicer, and 3-month-trial requirements are VA design choices in M26-4 Ch.22
limitation: Codified cite verified: bill Sec. 3(h) = 38 U.S.C. § 3737(h). Confirm UPB/rate caps against M26-4 Ch.22

claim_text: CARES Act forbearance was universal; only VA borrowers lost their same-rate exit.
definition: Civilian comparison: FHA/Fannie/Freddie kept a permanent same-rate exit
limitation: Lead argument; confirm the FHA/GSE deferral-exit citation before for-the-record use

claim_text: Biden's VA ended the COVID partial claim in Oct 2022; Trump's VA killed VASP in May 2025.
definition: Two-administrations framing; VASP killed effective 5/1/25 on ~8 days notice
limitation: Foreseeability, not intent; never assert intent to foreclose

claim_text: The VA takes about 75% of foreclosed veteran homes into its REO inventory.
definition: Auction.com data; +428% YoY auction supply
limitation: Industry data source; confirm current figure

claim_text: The VA says it helped 173,000 veterans avoid foreclosure in FY2025.
definition: VA's counter-number, stated in its own 6/15/26 launch press release
limitation: Verified that VA said it, not that 173,000 families kept their homes; lumps forbearances, higher-rate mods and short sales with retention; no bucket breakdown published

claim_text: The partial claim is not actually available until servicers implement it, deadline Nov 28, 2026.
definition: Two problems, prong 2: until a servicer publishes its own ETA, assume available nowhere
limitation: Available, not implemented

claim_text: The VA had separate authority all year to protect families immediately and chose not to use it.
definition: Part 36 tools + Section 3(h); the exclusion of displaced families is reversible without new legislation
limitation: Preempts VA's 'our hands are tied' deflection

claim_text: CBO projected $294 million in avoided foreclosure-related payments.
definition: Component of the fiscal case, H. Rept. 119-104
limitation: CBO estimate over the ten-year scoring window

claim_text: In November 2025 Congress expanded the Secretary's emergency authority to help veteran families before regulations issue.
definition: Pub. L. 119-37 §7307(e) removed the requirement that a loan have been in default on the day H.R. 1815 was signed; Secretary may issue administrative guidance for the Partial Claim Program and required loss-mitigation options, including any additional terms the Secretary determines necessary (38 U.S.C. §3737(h) as amended; 139 Stat. 651)
limitation: Statutory text as amended

claim_text: The program running today operates under exactly this authority: VA's June 1 2026 handbook is pre-regulation guidance invoking the Secretary's §3737 discretion.
definition: M26-4 Ch. 22 is pre-regulation guidance under §3737
limitation: Agency guidance, pre-rulemaking

claim_text: The Department cannot say it lacks authority to reach the families its eligibility barriers exclude; the barriers are handbook choices, reversible by the same pen that wrote them.
definition: Authority exists, Congress broadened it, and VA is actively using it for everyone except the families already harmed
limitation: Interpretation grounded in statute and agency guidance cited

claim_text: When VASP was cancelled, roughly 75,000 veteran borrowers were three or more payments behind; about 17,000 had been accepted into the program; 58,000+ had no path in.
definition: ICE Mortgage Technology via NPR 4/2/26 and CNN 4/30/25; only a servicer could submit a borrower, not the veteran
limitation: 58,000+ is derived by subtraction (75,000 minus ~17,000 accepted); labeled derived

claim_text: The partial-claim rule's only borrower-capacity test is whether the veteran can resume the scheduled monthly payment.
definition: 38 C.F.R. section 36.4803(d); no resolved-hardship condition (that belongs to the modification rule)
limitation: Rule text

claim_text: Loan modifications require a resolved hardship and cap the rate at one percent above the existing rate absent prior VA approval.
definition: 38 C.F.R. section 36.4315(a)(2) and (a)(8)
limitation: Rule text

claim_text: Regulation X required servicers to evaluate a complete application against all options in 30 days, give a specific reason per denial, and not dual-track.
definition: 12 C.F.R. section 1024.41(c)(1),(d),(f),(g); Not Reviewed is not a specific reason
limitation: Rule text, binding 2022-2026

claim_text: VA has described its loss-mitigation options as a hierarchy for review, and paid servicer incentives on it, since 2008.
definition: 38 C.F.R. section 36.4319(a)
limitation: Rule text

claim_text: VA built VALERI to determine servicer compliance and may inspect a servicer's complete delinquent-loan file on request.
definition: 38 C.F.R. section 36.4350(j); M26-4 Ch. 5 section 5.11
limitation: Rule/handbook text

claim_text: VA's April 2024 launch materials stated it had existing authority to establish VASP under 38 U.S.C. section 3732 and section 3720.
definition: Said twice in April 2024: launch materials, and on the record to HVAC 4/11/24 where Sec. McDonough described VASP as building on existing authority
limitation: Attribution: launched under Sec. McDonough, terminated 2025 under Sec. Collins; the existing-authority statement is the prior administration's

claim_text: Post-foreclosure evictions of veteran families are filed in the Secretary's name via a VA REO contractor under a federal contract with a ceiling near $374 million.
definition: VRM REO/eviction contract ceiling (USASpending/FPDS)
limitation: Contract record; confirm current ceiling

claim_text: The 180-day servicer implementation runway was the mortgage industry's own request, granted in full.
definition: MBA and CHLA each asked VA for at least 180 days in March 2026 comment letters; VA set exactly 180 days from the June 1 publication, landing 11/28/26
limitation: Industry letters reported by HousingWire 3/12/26; the 180-day figure is confirmed in VA's own servicer FAQ

claim_text: Foreclosure activity is climbing while the partial claim is still not running.
definition: 227,548 filings H1 2026 (+21% YoY, +28% vs H1 2024); VA delinquency 4.99% vs 2.75% conventional; industry forecast of FHA/VA foreclosures more than doubling by autumn 2027
limitation: ATTOM counts all residential property not veteran households; delinquency is survey data; the doubling figure is a practitioner forecast, cite as warning not projection

claim_text: The outcome was named in advance, repeatedly, by the industry, advocates, national press and Congress.
definition: Chronological warning record Mar 2025 - Jul 2026
limitation: Foreseeability, not intent; never cite as evidence that any official intended the outcome

claim_text: Low-income veteran households get inadequate or no professional legal help for the overwhelming majority of their civil legal problems.
definition: LSC 2017 Justice Gap: 71% had a civil legal problem; sought help for 21%; est. 88% received inadequate or no professional legal help
limitation: 2017 data, predates this crisis; measures civil legal need generally not foreclosure defence; veteran estimates based on fewer than 100 reported problems

claim_text: Families who took a COVID-19 forbearance were told, in VA's own guidance, that the missed payments would not have to be repaid in a single payment.
definition: VA CARES Act guidance: up to 180 days + 180 more on request; payments missed during forbearance do not have to be made up in a single payment
limitation: Guidance as issued in 2020; establishes what families were told, not what any servicer later offered

claim_text: The partial claim veterans used during the pandemic came from CARES Act authority that expired in 2021, leaving VA the only federal home loan program without one.
definition: H.R. 1815 sponsor summary: CARES partial-claim authority expired 2021; every other federal home loan program offers a partial claim except VA
limitation: Sponsor summary is an advocacy document; cite for legislative rationale on the record, not neutral analysis

claim_text: The bill that creates the VA partial claim also eliminates judicial review of VA's decision to take a secured interest in a veteran's defaulted home loan.
definition: CBO Mandates section: by not allowing judicial review of VA's decision to obtain secured interest in a veteran's defaulted home loan, the bill would eliminate an existing right of action; no cost assigned because judicial review does not result in monetary damages
limitation: Scores H.R. 1815 as reported in 2025; the authority was enacted via Pub. L. 119-37 s7307 and whether the enacted text carries the same provision is not verified here

claim_text: The partial claim was scored for roughly 12,200 claims averaging $27,200, with the authority expiring five years after enactment.
definition: CBO: ~12,200 partial claims at $27,200 average on VA-provided loan volume; 37% subsidy rate; $124M subsidy costs 2025-2035; authority expires five years after enactment; 25% cap or 30% if delinquent before May 1 2025
limitation: 12,200 is a take-up projection, not a statutory cap; scores H.R. 1815 as reported, not enacted Pub. L. 119-37; cohort tiers are counted differently

claim_text: VA's regulation pays a servicer at most $1,000 for a successful loss-mitigation outcome, and the largest incentive in the schedule is for a short sale.
definition: 38 CFR 36.4319(b) incentive schedule by tier: repayment plan 200/160/120/0; special forbearance same; loan modification 700/500/300/0; short sale 1000/800/600/0; deed-in-lieu 350/250/150/0; 36.4319(e) lets the Secretary stop payment for inadequate servicing
limitation: Incentives are one input into servicer behaviour, not the whole picture; tier ranking is itself a performance mechanism

claim_text: The money in VA's rules does not point toward keeping families in their homes.
definition: Top-tier modification pays the servicer $700 while CBO records VA typically pays lenders up to 25% of the outstanding balance on foreclosure (up to $75,000 on a $300,000 balance)
limitation: Our reading, not rule text; incentive goes to the servicer and guaranty to the holder, often but not always the same company; a guaranty payment reimburses loss rather than producing profit; not a finding that any servicer profits by foreclosing

claim_text: VA told Congress in February 2024 that it could not offer a partial claim, and explained the risk-share reason why.
definition: VA: unlike HUD and USDA it has no explicit authority to advance guaranty funds as loss mitigation and cannot offer a partial claim pulling from the guaranty; longstanding public position that Congress never authorized a partial advance without termination of the loan; lack of authority may be because VA carries only 25% of default risk where other federal programs carry 90% or more; COVID-VAPCP expired 10/28/2022
limitation: VA's position as of Feb 2024, before Congress created the permanent partial claim in Pub. L. 119-31 (7/30/25); explains the pre-2025 gap, not VA's authority today

claim_text: VA's own February 2024 numbers: more than 200,000 veterans affected by the COVID-19 emergency, more than 50,000 assisted through its temporary retention options.
definition: Also 145,000+ retained homes and avoided foreclosure over the prior year
limitation: VA's figures on VA's definitions; the 145,000 covers roughly the year to Feb 2024, a different period and measure from the 173,000 in the June 2026 launch release; cohort tiers are not derived from or merged with either

claim_text: A year before Congress acted, independent analysts had documented that VA had the most limited loss-mitigation options of any federal program and told Congress what was needed.
definition: Urban Institute 7/2024: VA has the most limited loss mitigation options lacking both portfolio and partial claim authority; Congress needs to grant VA partial claim authority and fund a fuller sequence of loss-mitigation options
limitation: Independent analysis not a government finding; the paper names funds acquired July 2021 and expired Oct 2022, and the Refund Modification operated on and off after the partial claim authority expired July 2022 - a run of short extensions rather than one end date; this site uses VA's own COVID-VAPCP expiry of 10/28/2022

claim_text: Uneven servicer implementation of VASP was predicted in print, before the harm, because VA never defined the standard servicers had to apply.
definition: Urban Institute 7/2024: lack of clear servicer guidance on 'exhausted all other options' gives servicers a good deal of discretion and assures implementation will be uneven; borrowers could not apply for VASP directly
limitation: A prediction about VASP as designed in 2024, published before VASP was terminated; evidence of foreseeability not a measurement of servicer behaviour

claim_text: Analysts noted at the time that VA could have built a more flexible modification under the authority it already had.
definition: Urban Institute 7/2024: VA with its existing authority could have introduced a more flexible modification rather than the flat 2.5 percent; proposed 20-25 percent payment-reduction target with a 2.5 percent floor at lower cost to government
limitation: Concerns VASP's 2024 design and the scope of VA's existing discretion; not a statement about the June 2026 partial-claim policy whose ceilings Congress set in statute

claim_text: VA's own borrower FAQ warned that short sale and deed in lieu could result in a loss or reduction in your future home loan benefit.
definition: CARES Act FAQ question 13 attaches the italicised future-benefit caution to short sale and deed in lieu
limitation: VA's statement of consequence in borrower guidance, not a finding about any family's entitlement

claim_text: Both COVID-era partial-claim options turned on a borrower's status in March 2020 and closed on fixed dates.
definition: COVID-VAPCP 7/27/21-10/28/22, current or within 30 days of current on 3/1/20; Refund Modification 7/27/21-7/1/23, within 120 days current on 3/1/20
limitation: Records the barriers as VA published them, not how many families they excluded

claim_text: Entry into CARES forbearance was mandatory on request, without documentation, regardless of whether the borrower was already behind.
definition: Interagency servicer fact sheet: servicer must give the forbearance requested; no documentation required; available regardless of delinquency status; VA servicers cannot require a lump sum immediately on exit
limitation: The duty attaches to entry and to the lump-sum prohibition on exit; it does not make any exit option mandatory

claim_text: VA instructed servicers not to start foreclosure or its alternatives at Step D, and recorded in the same circular that servicers had been doing exactly that.
definition: Circular 26-24-2: servicer is not to initiate foreclosure or alternatives at this point; VA observed servicers may have begun foreclosure or offered deed-in-lieu or short sale before VA had the opportunity to determine whether another option could help the borrower retain the home; all Step D loans to be referred to VA
limitation: VA's general observation about servicer conduct under earlier circulars, Feb 2024; not a finding about any individual servicer or loan

claim_text: The COVID-19 Home Retention Waterfall's own entry test was broader than the partial-claim test: current or less than 120 days past due as of March 1 2020, or a loan made on or after that date.
definition: Circular 26-24-2 section 5; Step C targets 31 pct of gross monthly household income without VA purchase exceeding 30 pct of UPB, and where achievable the servicer offers the Refund Modification regardless of the percentage of payment reduction
limitation: The waterfall entry test, distinct from the COVID-VAPCP test in C041; a borrower could fall outside one and inside the other

claim_text: In February 2024 VA told servicers it could purchase a delinquent loan outright under its section 3732 refunding authority.
definition: Step D options at VA's sole discretion include exercising loan refunding authority under 38 USC 3732 to purchase a delinquent loan from the holder and assume primary servicing
limitation: Describes what VA may do at its sole discretion; does not record how often it was used

claim_text: The servicer guidance said arrears could be paid back over time, and that a borrower could end a forbearance simply by resuming the regular monthly payment.
definition: Interagency CARES fact sheet: missed payments must be repaid although it may be paid back over time; inform borrowers they can resume making their regular monthly mortgage payment to end the forbearance and discuss repayment options; servicers of VA loans cannot require a lump sum immediately after exit; M26-4 Chapter 5 options
limitation: Records what the guidance instructed; not a finding that any particular servicer departed from it

claim_text: VA named its VASP authority on the record in February 2024, three months before launch: 38 U.S.C. 3732 and 38 C.F.R. Part 4320.
definition: Bell: 'Yes, sir, 38 USC 3732, as an authorization for VASP, as well as our current regulation at 38 CFR 4320'; 40,000 borrowers sought; 6 months of payments required on a modification in the waterfall
limitation: VA's assertion of authority, contested at the hearing by the subcommittee chair; records what VA claimed and when, not a finding that the authority existed; predates the April 2024 launch materials at C023 by three months

claim_text: The standard was set on the record, by the subcommittee's own chair: whether VA has authority to keep veterans in their homes is a veterans question, not a partisan one.
definition: Van Orden 2/15/24: 'I have concerns now, and I do not care who is in the White House, because this affects our veterans and is not political'; substantive objection was no statutory authority for a below-market-rate modification, very little confidence in VA's ability to administer, VA 'simply making this up'; VA answered 38 USC 3732 and 38 CFR 4320; program terminated eleven months later on ~8 days notice
limitation: The standard as stated at that hearing, quoted in full and in context; this project applies it to the entire record before and after January 2025 and to every party in it; it does not characterize any member's later positions or motives - what each party said and when is on News & Record and the Accountability Tracker

claim_text: Sixteen months before the replacement was terminated, Congress and VA were already arguing about the interest rate on a modification - from opposite directions.
definition: Chair pressed on intentional default for a lower payment, noting most veteran borrowers exceed 3%; Bell: almost 90% of portfolio at 2.5-3% coupon
limitation: Hearing record of a policy argument, not evidence about what any servicer offered any borrower; community-reported accounts of market-rate modification offers are recorded separately under their own label and not merged

claim_text: Veterans were told to pay the full arrears or lose the house, after VA had announced a foreclosure pause.
definition: Servicer: you have to pay the full amount back or you're going into foreclosure; pause message did not appear to be trickling down; ~$20,000 arrears
limitation: Press reporting of one family's account, not a finding about any servicer's conduct generally

claim_text: The alternative offered in place of a lump sum raised the monthly payment.
definition: Told arrears would move to the back end of a 30-year mortgage; then $57,000 demanded or a modification; modification raised payment $1,300/mo to $3,600
limitation: One family's reported terms; consistent with C033/C034 but not a pattern on its own

claim_text: VA active-foreclosure volume diverged from FHA and GSE volumes after the moratorium ended and VA's assistance program ended.
definition: NPR analysis of ICE data indexed to 100 in Jan 2018: VA ~123 by late 2023, FHA ~63, GSE ~55; chart marks VA ending its assistance program
limitation: News analysis of proprietary servicing data read from the published chart, so index values are approximate

claim_text: VA's 2023 foreclosure pause was temporary and ran only to May 31, 2024, with 40,000 VA borrowers in foreclosure or delinquent.
definition: Secretary: pause through May 31 2024 for the additional time that we need; 40,000 in foreclosure or delinquent without a modification; VA met with servicers of 90%+ of VA loans
limitation: Figures as reported Dec 2023; the 40,000 is point-in-time on the reporter's sourcing, not a VA publication, and is not merged with the cohort tiers

claim_text: On the government's own numbers, foreclosure is the spending and retention is the offset - the barriers that exclude the cohort move federal money to the more expensive outcome.
definition: CBO: decrease in net direct spending, $294M avoided foreclosure-related payments, ~$27,200 per claim; project model ~$2.3B to foreclose on the 31,500 in active foreclosure; 38 CFR 36.4319(b) caps retention incentive at $1,000 with largest incentive for short sale; VA REO eviction contract up to $374.4M
limitation: Project conclusion, not a government finding; $2.3B is our model from published per-foreclosure figures; CBO scores H.R. 1815 as reported; two of three official statements await Congressional Record or committee-video citation

claim_text: The committee that ended VASP argued for the partial claim on cost grounds - and put the arithmetic on the record.
definition: Apr 3 2025 joint statement: intent to establish a partial claim so veterans can stay in their homes 'while still protecting the American taxpayer'; $22,500 average delinquency vs $292,000 average loan purchased (now $320,000); a partial claim 'could solve the majority of delinquent loans at a much less expensive clip to the taxpayer'
limitation: The quoted words and figures are the committee majority's own; establishes the standard its authors set for themselves; the characterisation of why VASP was created is theirs, quoted not adopted

claim_text: Measured against the standard its own authors set, the partial claim has not yet done what it was said to do.
definition: VASP ended 5/1/25 on ~8 days notice; partial claim authorised 7/30/25, final policy 6/1/26, submissions 6/15/26, servicer deadline 11/28/26 - more than 18 months; Ch. 22 handbook barriers exclude the cohort the withdrawal exposed; CBO scored the partial claim as a decrease in net direct spending against ~$2.3B modelled for the 31,500 in active foreclosure
limitation: Project conclusion from the cited record, not a government finding; dated commitments measured against dated implementation; establishes that commitment and outcome diverged and who made the commitment, not why; $2.3B is this project's model

claim_text: Within six days of the VASP announcement, the ranking members of three committees of jurisdiction warned the Secretary in writing that the closure would push veterans into foreclosure.
definition: Apr 9 2025 letter signed by 22 Democrats and Independents; Takano's 80,000 figure the same month; Jul 2025 bipartisan bicameral statement describing the replacement as a tool to keep veterans in their homes
limitation: Statements of the members who made them, quoted as made; the 80,000 figure is Takano's and is not adopted or merged with the cohort tiers

claim_text: The Take Care of America's Veterans Act is paid for by raising VA home loan fees and by codifying future disability-rating cuts.
definition: IRRRL funding fee 0.5% to 1.42%; loan-assumption fee 0.5% to 1.0%; Section 108 codifies an estimated $57B in future rating reductions for tinnitus and sleep apnea; Common Defense estimates $8,000+ added over an average loan; VFW and DAV oppose the offsets; led by Reps. Bost and Van Orden and Sen. Moran
limitation: Records the offsets as written and the organisations' stated opposition; asserts no member's motive; the site's reading is labelled PROJECT ANALYSIS separately

claim_text: A family that took a loan modification in the previous 24 months does not qualify for the partial claim, and Congress did not write that rule.
definition: M26-4 Ch. 22 sec 22.02 a.7: "The borrower has not received a loan modification in the 24 months preceding the date the servicer evaluates the loan under the Waterfall." One of seven criteria in 22.02 that do not appear in 38 U.S.C. 3737.
limitation: Establishes that the criterion is an agency addition, not that it is unlawful. Does not establish how many families it excludes.

claim_text: The 24-month lockout runs to the date a servicer evaluates the loan, and servicers have until November 28 2026, so a family modified after roughly November 2024 is barred at the moment the program finally reaches them.
definition: The lookback in 22.02 a.7 is measured from "the date the servicer evaluates the loan under the Waterfall", not from the policy date. VA's servicer FAQ sets the operational deadline at 180 days from the June 1 2026 publication, November 28 2026.
limitation: Arithmetic from two published dates. Evaluation dates vary by servicer, and a family modified earlier may clear the lookback before their servicer is operational.

claim_text: Two of the ten qualifying criteria were changed or added after the public comment window closed, so the people who commented commented on a different document.
definition: Draft 22.02 a.7(a) required "at least six (6) monthly payments since the most recent modification"; the final replaced it with a flat 24-month lockout. Criterion 10, disqualifying a prior COVID-19 partial claim payment or refund modification, does not appear in the draft.
limitation: Establishes that the text changed between draft and final. Does not establish why, and does not establish that any commenter would have objected.

claim_text: A foreclosure protection Congress created in July 2025 was narrowed 105 days later, inside a funding bill.
definition: 38 U.S.C. 3720(h), created by Pub. L. 119-31 sec 2(b)(3), barred the Secretary from acting under 3720(a)(2) to (5) "before the completion of the sequence of mitigation options". Pub. L. 119-37 sec 7307(a) replaced that with a bar applying only to a purchase under 3732(a)(2) "unless the Secretary determines the purchase would be made consistent with section 3732(d)". The companion bar in 3732(d) was left intact.
limitation: Compares enacted text with amended text. Does not assert intent, does not assert that the change caused any foreclosure, and no committee report or explanatory statement examining this specific effect has been located as of 2026-08-18.

claim_text: Of thirteen recommendations one veteran family submitted on VA's draft policy, VA adopted two, and both were drafting changes rather than enforcement or remedy.
definition: A public comment on the draft M26-4 Chapters 5 and 22 was filed on March 11 2026; VA acknowledged receipt by email the same day. Each of the thirteen recommendations was compared against the text of the June 1 2026 final policy. Two were adopted: the 30 percent COVID-era cap applied by reference to when a payment was missed, and a 30-day VALERI submission clock. The eleven declined are each either an enforcement mechanism that would constrain a servicer or a remedy that would reach a family already harmed.
limitation: Measures one commenter's recommendations against the final text. It does not measure what VA did with the rest of the comment record, which we have not reviewed, and it does not assert that VA read or considered this comment specifically. PUBLISHED 2026-08-31 in redacted form at /docs/public-comment/, so both columns of the table are now checkable by a reader. COUNT, stated because both numbers appear on this site: the comment makes twelve section-by-section recommendations and one cross-cutting ask under 38 U.S.C. 3737(h). This row counts thirteen by including the cross-cutting ask; the comment's own text says twelve, meaning the section items. Neither is wrong. VERSION: the published copy is the author's tightened copy dated 2026-03-16, five days after filing; 194 of about 240 sentences are identical to the copy dated 2026-03-11 and the differences are added citation detail. It is not offered as a byte-exact reproduction of what VA received.

claim_text: Federal law sets six conditions a VA refinance must meet before it can be guaranteed, and each one can be checked from a family's own closing papers.
definition: 38 U.S.C. 3709 sets four of them: the lender must certify a recoupment period and schedule all fees and incurred costs to be recouped within 36 months of loan issuance (a); it must provide the borrower with a net tangible benefit test (b)(1); the new rate must be at least 50 basis points below the old one where a fixed rate replaces a fixed rate and 200 basis points where an adjustable rate replaces a fixed rate (b)(2) and (b)(3); and the loan may not be guaranteed until the later of six consecutive monthly payments made on the loan being refinanced and 210 days after that loan's first payment due date (c). 38 CFR 36.4307 adds that the new monthly principal and interest payment must be lower and caps the new loan at the refinanced balance plus authorised closing costs and a discount of no more than 2 percent. VA Circular 26-19-22 requires the lender to twice present the veteran with a comparison of the two loans, once within three business days of application and again at closing.
limitation: Quotes the statute, the regulation and the circular as published. Whether any particular refinance met them is a legal question, and most of the documents that answer it sit in the lender's loan file rather than the family's.

claim_text: VA's Inspector General reported that the Loan Guaranty Service could not confirm lenders were meeting three of those requirements.
definition: VA OIG Report 21-01295-149, August 23 2023, page ii: Prior to these new controls, LGY was unable to sufficiently ensure those three requirements were met. The three are fee recoupment, net tangible benefit and loan seasoning. On the reporting lenders owe VA after closing, page iii: lenders did not comply, and LGY's controls were not sufficient for obtaining compliance.
limitation: The finding describes controls in place before the May 2020 controls the audit describes, and the audit sample is fiscal year 2020. The OIG made nine recommendations and VBA concurred with all nine; three were flagged as needing a VA Office of General Counsel legal opinion before a disagreement about closing costs could be resolved.

claim_text: Thousands of veterans were overcharged on VA refinances in the year those refinances multiplied nearly sevenfold.
definition: VA OIG Report 21-01295-149. Page 1: In fiscal year (FY) 2020, VA reported a 598 percent increase in the number of IRRRLs from the previous year. Page ii: the OIG estimated that at least 3,200 FY 2020 borrowers were overcharged $1.6 million. Page 19: approximately 18,400 of the FY 2020 borrowers (21 percent) were potentially overcharged a total of $3 million in unsupported, unallowable or unreasonable closing costs.
limitation: Both figures are statistical estimates projected from audit samples of fiscal year 2020 loans, not counts of identified individuals. The $1.6 million estimate rests on 19 sampled loans. VA and the OIG did not agree on part of the closing-cost finding.

claim_text: In 2019 VA's Inspector General found the Loan Guaranty Service did not always oversee servicers well enough for borrowers in default to get the help they were owed.
definition: VA OIG Report 18-03979-204, September 30 2019: The OIG found the Loan Guaranty Service did not always provide sufficient oversight to ensure borrowers in default received the needed assistance. And: The audit team estimated, based on a sample review of 200 loans, that 14 percent of loans had at least one oversight deficiency. All four recommendations are recorded as Closed-Implemented, the last of them on June 23 2020.
limitation: A 2019 audit projected from a 200-loan sample. Closure records that VA satisfied the OIG it had acted on a recommendation; it does not measure what happened to families afterwards. The four closure dates differ; the private appendix this row was built from records them all as June 23 2020, which the OIG dashboard does not support.

claim_text: In 2022 the Inspector General told VBA leadership that its focus on organisational problems had harmed some veterans, and VBA formally disagreed in writing.
definition: VA OIG Management Advisory Memorandum 22-01290-237, December 8 2022, page 2: VBA's well-intentioned focus on solving organizational challenges has, however, resulted in negative consequences for some veterans and their families. Page 7 records the response: VBA strongly oppose[s] the implication that VBA did not always fully consider the effect organizational decisions would have on Veterans, beneficiaries, and their families.
limitation: The memo is cross-cutting across VBA, drawing on at least four reports issued since 2018 covering home loan funding fees, pensions, personal information and medical examinations. It is not a Loan Guaranty finding and it makes no new recommendations.

claim_text: A state attorney general has already enforced against a mortgage servicer for failing to apply COVID-era protections correctly.
definition: On December 17 2025 the Massachusetts Attorney General announced a $4.65 million settlement with Newrez LLC, as successor by merger to Specialized Loan Servicing LLC, under the headline AG Campbell Reaches $4.65 Million Settlement with Mortgage Loan Servicer for Unlawful Foreclosures and Deceptive Business Practices, subtitled Violations Include Failure to Correctly Implement Covid-Era Protections.
limitation: A state settlement under Massachusetts consumer protection law. It is not a VA loan case, it binds no other state or company, and a settlement is not an admission. The company is named here as the subject of a published enforcement action, not as the subject of an argument.

claim_text: A federal appeals court has held that the company servicing a loan when an escrow payment comes due is the one responsible for making it.
definition: Harrell v. Freedom Mortgage Corp., No. 19-1379 (4th Cir. Oct. 2, 2020), published: the person responsible for servicing the mortgage at the time a payment is due must make that payment. The opinion ties that duty to the date the payment becomes due, and reads the Regulation X standard at 12 C.F.R. 1024.17(k)(1) so that timely manner means on or before the deadline to avoid a penalty.
limitation: Published Fourth Circuit precedent, binding in Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia and West Virginia and persuasive elsewhere. The company in the case name is part of the citation, not the subject of this claim.

claim_text: Washington's own financial regulator led a national mortgage servicing settlement in 2020 and charged another servicer in 2026.
definition: On December 7 2020 the Washington State Department of Financial Institutions announced the finalised multistate resolution with Nationstar Mortgage LLC, doing business as Mr. Cooper: consumer redress approaching $90 million to more than 115,000 consumers in 53 states, plus penalties in excess of $6.5 million, over conduct including missed tax payments from borrower escrow accounts, failure to terminate private mortgage insurance when conditions were met, and wrongful foreclosures. DFI led the investigation alongside 52 state regulators, 51 state attorneys general and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. On April 6 2026 the same department issued a statement of charges against Newrez LLC seeking $4,175,000, alleging among other things failing to mediate in good faith during foreclosure and improperly maintained and serviced escrow accounts.
limitation: State licensing and consumer protection enforcement over mortgage servicing conduct generally. Neither action is a VA loan case. The 2026 charges are allegations; a statement of charges is not a finding.

claim_text: A family whose servicer modified their loan in the previous 24 months is barred from the partial claim by a rule Congress never wrote, and the clock runs to a date the servicer controls.
definition: M26-4 Chapter 22, final, effective June 1 2026, criterion 22.02 a.7, verbatim: The borrower has not received a loan modification in the 24 months preceding the date the servicer evaluates the loan under the Waterfall. The lookback therefore ends on the date of the servicer's evaluation, not on any date the family controls. 38 U.S.C. 3737(a) sets three conditions and contains no lookback of any length and no reference to a prior loan modification. The February 2026 draft had no such criterion; its criterion 7(a) asked only that a modified loan have six monthly payments since the most recent modification.
limitation: Compares handbook text with statutory text. It establishes that the lookback is an agency addition and that its end date is set by the servicer, not that it is unlawful.

claim_text: Congress made the loss mitigation sequence mandatory; VA's handbook makes the foreclosure halt wait until a trial payment plan is offered.
definition: 38 U.S.C. 3732(d), added by Pub. L. 119-31 section 2(a)(3) on July 30 2025, verbatim: The Secretary shall prescribe loss mitigation procedures, including a mandatory sequence in which the holder of a loan guaranteed under this chapter shall offer loss mitigation options (including an option to enter into a partial claim agreement under the VA Home Loan Program Reform Act) to a veteran, to help prevent the foreclosure of such loan. The Secretary may not purchase an entire such loan until the veteran has completed such sequence. It names no trial payment plan. M26-4 Chapter 22 section 22.03 a.2, final, verbatim: Servicers must cease initiating, continuing, or completing foreclosures on loans where a TPP is offered to the borrower. Section 22.03 a: Servicers will only offer a TPP when the qualifying criteria are met. So the halt is conditional on all ten criteria.
limitation: Quotes the statute and the handbook. It establishes what triggers the halt on paper; it does not establish what any servicer did in any case, and it does not assert that the handbook is unlawful.

claim_text: VA's partial claim chapter recognises a spouse when the marriage ends or the borrower dies, and not while the household is intact.
definition: M26-4 Chapter 22, final, effective June 1 2026, searched in full on 2026-08-21: the chapter contains no occurrence of the words co-borrower, caregiver or household. It addresses family circumstance only as exceptions to a rule written about one borrower: a former spouse who received the property through a divorce (22.02 a.8(a)), a surviving spouse who received it from the estate (a.8(b)), a Successor in Interest who assumed the loan before the default (a.8(c)), a borrower deployed, hospitalised or in long-term care, where occupancy is met if the property is a family member's primary residence (a.3(c)), and a co-obligor whose signature is waived because they committed domestic violence (a.9(d)). Eligibility itself is decided on one borrower and that borrower's residence.
limitation: A stated negative: three words are absent from one chapter, verified by a full-text search of the final. It is a finding about the program's drafting, not about how any servicer applies it, and not about any one family. It does not assert that a caregiver spouse on the note is excluded in practice, only that the chapter never names the arrangement.

claim_text: Eleven days after VA announced the end of VASP, the mortgage industry told the Secretary in writing that thousands of veterans who might qualify had not completed the loss-mitigation sequence, and asked VA to let borrowers fix a defective application rather than deny one filed on time.
definition: CHLA to Secretary Doug Collins, April 14 2025: "There are likely thousands (maybe tens of thousands) of veterans who may qualify for VASP who haven't gone through the waterfall, and many who have been told they meet VASP qualifications but have not fully submitted documents to VA (and may not be able to within two weeks)." The letter asks that "if there is key information missing from an existing application (or an issue with title, etc), VA should give the veteran and their servicer time to cure the fault if the application was submitted on time, rather than just deny the file," and requests a 60-day transition after formal publication.
limitation: A trade association's letter, not a government finding, and it does not establish that VA declined any specific application. What it establishes is that the risk was put to the Secretary in writing, by the industry that would have to administer the deadline, before the deadline ran.
